name: Information Security Policy
description: Overall framework for protecting the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information.
purpose: establish the framework, principles and mandatory requirements for protecting the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information and information systems
objectives: Protect information assets against unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration and loss.
Define clear accountability for information security across the organization.
Ensure security requirements are applied consistently to systems, data and people.
Provide a basis for measuring and improving the security posture.
principles: Security measures are proportionate to the sensitivity of the information and the risks it faces.
Access is granted on the basis of least privilege and business need.
Security is a shared responsibility of everyone who handles the organization's information.
Controls are layered so that the failure of one does not expose the information.

definitions.Information asset: Any information, or system that stores or processes it, that has value to the organization.
definitions.Confidentiality: Ensuring information is accessible only to those authorized to see it.
definitions.Integrity: Safeguarding the accuracy and completeness of information.
definitions.Availability: Ensuring authorized users can access information when they need it.
definitions.Control: A measure that reduces the likelihood or impact of a risk.

monitoring: Security controls are reviewed periodically for design and operating effectiveness.
Security metrics and open findings are reported to management.
Non-compliance is investigated and may lead to corrective or disciplinary action.

name: Access Control Policy
description: Rules for granting, reviewing and revoking access to systems and information.
purpose: define how access to information and systems is requested, approved, granted, reviewed and removed so that only authorized individuals have the access they need
objectives: Ensure access to systems and data is authorized, appropriate and traceable to an individual.
Enforce least privilege and segregation of duties.
Detect and remove access that is no longer required.
Reduce the risk of unauthorized access through strong authentication.
principles: Access is denied by default and granted only on documented business need.
Every account is attributable to a named individual or a documented service owner.
Privileged access is separated from day-to-day access and is kept to a minimum.
Access rights are reviewed regularly and removed promptly when no longer needed.

definitions.Least privilege: Granting only the minimum access needed to perform a role.
definitions.Privileged account: An account with elevated rights, such as administrator or root.
definitions.Multi-factor authentication: Verifying identity with two or more independent factors.
definitions.Access review: A periodic check that users' access rights remain appropriate.
definitions.Segregation of duties: Dividing tasks so that no single person can complete a sensitive process alone.

monitoring: Access reviews are completed at the defined frequency and their results retained as evidence.
Authentication and privileged activity logs are monitored for anomalies.
Exceptions such as shared or dormant accounts are tracked to closure.

name: Risk Management Policy
description: Approach to identifying, assessing, treating and monitoring risk.
purpose: set out how risks are identified, assessed, treated, monitored and reported so that they are managed within the organization's risk appetite
objectives: Identify and record risks to the organization's objectives, information and services.
Assess risks consistently using a defined scoring method.
Treat risks that exceed the organization's risk appetite and assign owners for each.
Give management timely visibility of the risk profile.
principles: Risk management is part of everyday decision-making, not a separate exercise.
Every risk has a named owner who is accountable for its treatment.
Risks are assessed with a consistent, documented method so results are comparable.
Risk acceptance is an explicit, recorded decision made at the right level of authority.

definitions.Risk: The effect of uncertainty on objectives, expressed as a combination of likelihood and impact.
definitions.Inherent risk: The level of risk before controls are taken into account.
definitions.Residual risk: The level of risk remaining after controls are applied.
definitions.Risk appetite: The amount of risk the organization is willing to accept in pursuit of its objectives.
definitions.Risk treatment: The action taken to modify a risk: mitigate, transfer, avoid or accept.

monitoring: The risk register is reviewed at the defined frequency and after significant change.
Treatment actions are tracked to completion and overdue actions are escalated.
Risk reports are presented to management, highlighting risks above appetite.

name: Data Privacy Policy
description: How personal data is collected, used, shared and retained, and how individuals' rights are respected.
purpose: describe how personal data is collected, used, shared, retained and protected, and how the rights of individuals are respected
objectives: Handle personal data fairly, transparently and only for stated purposes.
Collect and keep no more personal data than is necessary.
Enable individuals to exercise their rights over their personal data.
Protect personal data against unauthorized access, loss or disclosure.
principles: Personal data is processed only for specified and legitimate purposes.
Privacy is considered from the start of any new system, process or project.
Personal data is kept accurate and retained only as long as necessary.
Individuals are told how their personal data is used.

definitions.Personal data: Any information relating to an identified or identifiable individual.
definitions.Data subject: The individual to whom personal data relates.
definitions.Processing: Any operation performed on personal data, such as collection, storage, use or deletion.
definitions.Consent: A freely given, specific and informed indication of an individual's agreement to processing.
definitions.Privacy breach: An event leading to unauthorized access to, or loss or disclosure of, personal data.

monitoring: Records of processing and consent are maintained and reviewed.
Requests from individuals are logged and tracked against response deadlines.
Privacy practices are checked periodically against this policy.

name: Data Protection Policy
description: Technical and organizational safeguards for data throughout its lifecycle.
purpose: define the safeguards applied to data throughout its lifecycle, from creation and classification to storage, transmission and disposal
objectives: Ensure data is classified and handled according to its sensitivity.
Protect data at rest and in transit against unauthorized access and leakage.
Retain data only as long as required and dispose of it securely.
Control how data is shared inside and outside the organization.
principles: The level of protection matches the classification of the data.
Sensitive data is encrypted wherever it is stored or transmitted.
Data owners are accountable for the data in their care.
Data that is no longer needed is securely disposed of.

definitions.Data classification: Assigning data to a category that determines how it must be handled.
definitions.Data owner: The person accountable for a set of data and decisions about its use.
definitions.Encryption: Encoding data so only authorized parties can read it.
definitions.Data at rest: Data held in storage, such as on disks, databases or backups.

monitoring: Classification and encryption coverage are reviewed periodically.
Data loss events and policy violations are logged and investigated.
Retention and disposal activities are evidenced.

name: Vendor Management Policy
description: How third-party suppliers are assessed, contracted, monitored and offboarded.
purpose: define how third-party vendors are assessed, contracted, monitored and offboarded so that the risks they introduce are understood and controlled
objectives: Understand and control the security risks introduced by third parties.
Ensure vendors are assessed before engagement and at regular intervals.
Embed security and data protection obligations in vendor contracts.
Ensure access and data are recovered when a vendor relationship ends.
principles: The depth of vendor assessment is proportionate to the criticality of the service and the data involved.
The organization remains accountable for its information even when a vendor processes it.
Security obligations are agreed in writing before a vendor is given access.
Vendor risk is monitored for the whole life of the relationship.

definitions.Vendor: An external organization that supplies goods or services, including cloud and outsourced service providers.
definitions.Due diligence: The assessment of a vendor's security and suitability before and during an engagement.
definitions.Critical vendor: A vendor whose failure or compromise would significantly affect operations or sensitive data.
definitions.Service level agreement: The agreed measures of a vendor's service performance.
definitions.Offboarding: The controlled ending of a vendor relationship, including return of data and removal of access.

monitoring: A register of vendors, their criticality and assessment status is maintained.
Vendor assessments and contract obligations are tracked against due dates.
Vendor incidents and performance issues are reported to management.

name: Cloud Security Policy
description: Security requirements for adopting and operating cloud services.
purpose: set the security requirements for selecting, configuring and operating cloud services so that data and workloads in the cloud are protected
objectives: Ensure cloud services are approved, configured securely and operated under clear ownership.
Protect data stored and processed in the cloud.
Prevent and detect cloud misconfiguration.
Maintain visibility of activity in cloud environments.
principles: Security responsibilities shared with the cloud provider are understood and documented.
Cloud resources are deployed from approved, secure configurations.
Nothing is exposed to the internet unless there is an approved business need.
Cloud activity is logged and monitored.

definitions.Cloud service: Computing resources delivered over a network by a provider, such as IaaS, PaaS or SaaS.
definitions.Shared responsibility model: The division of security duties between the cloud provider and the customer.
definitions.Misconfiguration: A setting that unintentionally weakens security, such as publicly accessible storage.
definitions.Identity and access management: The control of who can do what in a cloud environment.
definitions.Workload: An application or service running on cloud resources.

monitoring: Cloud configurations are checked against the approved baseline.
Cloud audit logs are retained and reviewed.
Findings from configuration checks are tracked to remediation.

name: Incident Management Policy
description: How security incidents are detected, reported, handled and learned from.
purpose: define how information security incidents are detected, reported, assessed, contained, resolved and reviewed
objectives: Detect and report incidents quickly.
Limit the impact of incidents through a consistent response.
Preserve evidence and meet notification obligations.
Learn from incidents to prevent recurrence.
principles: Everyone has a duty to report suspected incidents without delay.
Response is prioritized by severity and business impact.
Actions taken during an incident are recorded.
Every significant incident is followed by a review.

definitions.Security incident: An event that compromises, or threatens to compromise, the confidentiality, integrity or availability of information.
definitions.Containment: Action taken to stop an incident from spreading or causing further harm.
definitions.Root cause: The underlying reason an incident occurred.
definitions.Severity: A rating of how serious an incident is, used to prioritize the response.
definitions.Post-incident review: A structured review of an incident and the response to it.

monitoring: Incidents are logged with their severity, timeline and outcome.
Response times are measured against the defined targets.
Actions from post-incident reviews are tracked to completion.

name: Password Policy
description: Rules for creating, protecting and managing passwords and other authentication secrets.
purpose: define the rules for creating, protecting and managing passwords and other authentication secrets
objectives: Ensure passwords are strong enough to resist guessing and brute-force attacks.
Prevent passwords from being shared, exposed or reused.
Limit the damage from a compromised password.
Strengthen authentication beyond passwords where the risk warrants it.
principles: Passwords are confidential to the individual they are issued to.
Length matters more than complexity alone.
A password is never the only protection for sensitive or privileged access.
Compromised or suspected-compromised passwords are changed immediately.

definitions.Password: A secret string used to prove identity.
definitions.Passphrase: A longer password made of several words.
definitions.Multi-factor authentication: Verifying identity with two or more independent factors.
definitions.Account lockout: Temporarily disabling an account after repeated failed sign-in attempts.
definitions.Password manager: An approved tool that securely stores and generates passwords.

monitoring: Password settings are enforced technically and checked against this policy.
Failed sign-in and lockout events are monitored.
Accounts with non-compliant settings are identified and corrected.

name: Acceptable Use Policy
description: What users may and may not do with the organization's systems, devices and information.
purpose: explain what is and is not acceptable when using the organization's systems, devices, networks and information
objectives: Set clear expectations for the use of the organization's technology and information.
Protect the organization and its users from misuse.
Reduce security incidents caused by unsafe behaviour.
Make users aware that use may be monitored.
principles: Systems and information are provided for business purposes.
Users are accountable for activity carried out under their accounts.
Users behave lawfully, ethically and with respect for others.
If in doubt about whether something is acceptable, users ask before acting.

definitions.User: Anyone who uses the organization's systems or information, including employees, contractors and temporary staff.
definitions.Organizational resources: Systems, devices, networks, accounts and information provided by the organization.
definitions.Personal use: Use of organizational resources for non-business purposes.
definitions.Removable media: Portable storage such as USB drives and external disks.

monitoring: Use of systems may be monitored in line with applicable law and internal rules.
Users acknowledge this policy when they are given access.
Violations are handled through the disciplinary process.

name: Business Continuity Policy
description: How the organization prepares for, responds to and recovers from disruption.
purpose: set out how the organization prepares for, responds to and recovers from disruptive events so that critical services continue
objectives: Identify critical services and the resources they depend on.
Define recovery objectives for critical services.
Maintain plans that enable recovery within those objectives.
Prove the plans work through regular testing.
principles: The safety of people comes first in any disruption.
Recovery priorities follow business impact.
Plans are kept current, accessible and tested.
Lessons from tests and real events are fed back into the plans.

definitions.Business continuity: The capability to continue delivering services at acceptable levels during a disruption.
definitions.Business impact analysis: Assessing the effect of disruption on activities over time.
definitions.Recovery time objective: The target time to restore a service after disruption.
definitions.Recovery point objective: The maximum tolerable period of data loss.
definitions.Disaster recovery: Restoring technology systems and data after a disruption.

monitoring: Plans are reviewed and tested at the defined frequency.
Test results and corrective actions are recorded and tracked.
Readiness is reported to management.

name: Asset Management Policy
description: How information and technology assets are inventoried, owned, used and disposed of.
purpose: define how information and technology assets are identified, inventoried, assigned an owner, protected and disposed of
objectives: Maintain an accurate inventory of information and technology assets.
Assign an accountable owner to every asset.
Protect assets according to their value and sensitivity.
Dispose of assets securely at the end of their life.
principles: An asset that is not known cannot be protected.
Every asset has an owner.
Assets are returned when they are no longer needed by their holder.
Data is removed from assets before disposal or reuse.

definitions.Asset: Anything of value to the organization, including hardware, software, data and services.
definitions.Asset owner: The person accountable for an asset throughout its life.
definitions.Asset inventory: The record of the organization's assets and their attributes.
definitions.Decommissioning: Retiring an asset from service in a controlled way.
definitions.Sanitization: Removing data from an asset so it cannot be recovered.

monitoring: The asset inventory is reconciled periodically against what is actually in use.
Assets without an owner or past end of support are reported.
Disposal is evidenced with records of sanitization.

name: Change Management Policy
description: How changes to systems and services are requested, assessed, approved and implemented.
purpose: ensure changes to systems, applications and infrastructure are requested, assessed, approved, tested and implemented in a controlled way
objectives: Reduce disruption and security incidents caused by change.
Ensure changes are assessed and approved before implementation.
Ensure changes are tested and can be reversed.
Keep an auditable record of what changed, when and why.
principles: No change is made to production without authorization.
The person who requests or builds a change does not approve it alone.
Every change has a tested way back.
Emergency changes follow the same rules, compressed, and are reviewed afterwards.

definitions.Change: The addition, modification or removal of anything that could affect a system or service.
definitions.Change request: The formal record proposing a change.
definitions.Change advisory board: The group that assesses and advises on changes.
definitions.Emergency change: A change that must be made urgently to restore service or prevent serious harm.
definitions.Rollback: Returning a system to its state before a change.

monitoring: Changes are sampled to confirm they were approved and tested.
Failed and unauthorized changes are recorded and investigated.
Change metrics are reported to management.

name: Backup and Recovery Policy
description: How data is backed up, protected and restored.
purpose: define how data and systems are backed up, how backups are protected and tested, and how they are restored when needed
objectives: Ensure data can be recovered after loss, corruption or attack.
Meet the organization's recovery objectives.
Protect backups from unauthorized access and tampering.
Prove recoverability through regular restore tests.
principles: A backup is only as good as its last successful restore test.
Backups are kept separate from the systems they protect.
Backups receive the same protection as the data they contain.
Backup failures are treated as incidents and resolved promptly.

definitions.Backup: A copy of data kept so it can be restored after loss.
definitions.Recovery point objective: The maximum tolerable period of data loss.
definitions.Recovery time objective: The target time to restore a service.
definitions.Restore test: A test that data can actually be recovered from a backup.
definitions.Offsite backup: A backup stored at a different location from the original data.

monitoring: Backup job results are monitored and failures followed up.
Restore tests are performed at the defined frequency and recorded.
Backup coverage is reviewed when systems are added or changed.

name: Remote Work Security Policy
description: Security requirements for working outside the organization's premises.
purpose: set the security requirements for working outside the organization's premises, including home and mobile working
objectives: Give remote workers secure access to the systems they need.
Protect organizational information on devices and networks outside the organization's control.
Ensure remote workers know their security responsibilities.
Ensure lost or stolen devices are reported and handled quickly.
principles: The same level of security applies wherever work is done.
Remote connections to internal systems are authenticated and encrypted.
Organizational information stays on approved devices and services.
Remote workers take reasonable care to keep information from being overseen or overheard.

definitions.Remote work: Work carried out away from the organization's premises.
definitions.Virtual private network: An encrypted connection to the organization's network.
definitions.Bring your own device: Using a personally owned device for work.
definitions.Public network: A network not controlled by the organization or the user, such as public Wi-Fi.
definitions.Approved device: A device that meets the organization's security requirements and is authorized for work.

monitoring: Remote connections are logged and monitored.
Devices used for remote work are checked for compliance with security requirements.
Lost and stolen device reports are tracked to closure.
